summary: Maastricht University's NL-High Potential scholarship offers 18 full scholarships for 2027–28 to talented students from outside the EU/EEA on selected master's programmes. It covers tuition, living expenses, insurance and visa costs.
covers: Living expenses: €15,925 for a 13-month programme or €30,625 for a 25-month programme.
Health and liability insurance (€700), visa application costs, and pre-academic training costs.
eligibility: Nationality of a country outside the EU/EEA, Switzerland and Suriname, and eligibility for a Dutch entry visa and residence permit.
Excellent results: a GPA of at least 7.5 out of 10 (or equivalent) on your latest transcript.
A complete application to a participating full-time master's programme — only programmes on the scholarship's list qualify.
how_to_apply: Check the list of participating master's programmes for 2027–28.
Submit a complete master's application, meeting all admission requirements, by 10 December 2026.
Apply for the scholarship between 1 October 2026 and 1 February 2027 (23:59).
Make your motivation specific to Maastricht's problem-based learning and your programme.
watch_out: Two deadlines: the master's application (10 December) comes well before the scholarship deadline (1 February). Missing the first rules you out.
Only certain programmes take part; check the list before you choose.
Eighteen awards across all eligible countries makes this very competitive — apply for other scholarships in parallel.

sources.title: Maastricht University — Scholarships for talented students

costs: The scholarship — a full fee waiver
Living costs: €15,925 for a 13-month programme or €30,625 for a 25-month programme
Health and liability insurance, the visa application and pre-academic training
documents: A CV of no more than two A4 pages, including any awards or prizes
A motivation letter written on Maastricht's template
Your latest transcript showing a GPA of 7.5 out of 10 or higher, plus a document explaining your grading system
A personal statement of financial need — for example financial difficulty, caring duties, a disability or refugee status
One reference letter from a (former) professor, lecturer or employer, dated February 2026 or later and following the scholarship's referee guidelines — you upload it yourself

faq.a: Each faculty ranks its top five applicants and sends them to the International Services Desk for a final check in March 2027. Selected candidates are then invited to an online interview.

faq.q: I already have a master's degree. Can I apply?
faq.a: Yes, but preference goes to candidates who have not yet obtained a master's degree.

faq.q: Can my referee send the letter directly?
faq.a: No. You upload the reference letter yourself, and letters that ignore the guidelines leave your application incomplete.
